result: MIR156A and MIR156C have dominant roles within the miR156 family in Arabidopsis, as demonstrated by the mir156a mir156c double mutant showing shortened juvenile phase (2.1 plastochrons earlier abaxial trichome appearance) and earlier flowering compared to wild type.

result: Sugar specifically represses miR156 expression, with glucose playing a major role. Sucrose, glucose, and maltose reduce miR156 levels within 30 minutes, while fructose and mannitol do not. Sugar starvation increases miR156, and the effect is specific to miR156 (not other miRNAs tested).
status_reasoning: Claims C18-C24 collectively demonstrate sugar-specific repression of miR156 through multiple complementary experiments: sugar treatment (C18-C22), starvation (C23), and specificity controls (C24). The rapid response (30 min) and specificity strengthen the conclusion.

result: Sugar from pre-existing leaves acts as a mobile signal to repress miR156 and trigger juvenile-to-adult phase transition. result: Sugar regulates miR156 at both transcriptional and post-transcriptional levels. Glucose reduces RNA Pol II binding at MIR156 promoters (transcriptional) and promotes degradation of pri-MIR156 transcripts even when transcription is blocked by ActD (post-transcriptional), independently of miRNA processing machinery.

result: Sugar-induced pri-MIR156C degradation requires de novo protein synthesis but occurs independently of canonical nonsense-mediated decay (NMD), as shown by cycloheximide and upf mutant experiments.

result: The gradual increase in sugar after seed germination serves as an endogenous developmental timing cue.
